title: The scalar localization of a linear category is a linear category
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\varpi\in R$, $R[1/\varpi]$ the localization of $R$ at $\varpi$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and $\mathcal C$ an $R$-linear category [def-weil-linear-category]. For objects $K,L$ put $H(K,L)=\Hom_{\mathcal C}(K,L)\otimes_RR[1/\varpi]$, the base change of the $R$-module $\Hom_{\mathcal C}(K,L)$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. Then: (1) for objects $K,L,M$ there is a unique $R[1/\varpi]$-bilinear map $\circ:H(L,M)\times H(K,L)\to H(K,M)$ with $(f\otimes a)\circ(g\otimes b)=(f\circ g)\otimes ab$; (2) this composition is associative and $\mathrm{id}_K\otimes1$ is a two-sided identity, so the objects of $\mathcal C$ with the $R[1/\varpi]$-modules $H(K,L)$ form an $R[1/\varpi]$-linear category $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$; (3) $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$, identity on objects and $f\mapsto f\otimes1$ on morphisms, is a functor and is $R$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor] for the $R$-linear structure of $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ obtained by restriction of scalars along $R\to R[1/\varpi]$; (4) if $T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ is an automorphism of categories that is $R$-linear, then $K\mapsto T(K)$, $f\otimes a\mapsto T(f)\otimes a$ is a well-defined $R[1/\varpi]$-linear automorphism $T'$ of $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ (with inverse induced by $T^{-1}$), and $Q\circ T=T'\circ Q$.

proof.text: Write $A=R[1/\varpi]$. Its ring map $R\to A$ and commutative ring structure are supplied by [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Composition $\beta(f,g)=f\circ g$ in $\mathcal C$ is $R$-bilinear by [def-weil-linear-category]. Apply the bilinear extension clause of [def-weil-module-base-change] to the three Hom modules. It gives exactly the unique $A$-bilinear composition with $(f\otimes a)\circ(g\otimes b)=(f\circ g)\otimes ab$, proving (1).

proof.text: For the remaining calculations, every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors: from the defining presentation of a tensor product as the free $R$-module on pairs modulo the additive and balancing relations (Stacks 00CX), a representative is a finite sum $\sum_i r_i(m_i\otimes a_i)=\sum_i m_i\otimes (r_i a_i)$. Thus additivity extends an equality on pure tensors to all inputs, one input at a time. For $u=\sum_i f_i\otimes a_i$, $v=\sum_j g_j\otimes b_j$, $w=\sum_k h_k\otimes c_k$ with consecutive sources and targets, $(u\circ v)\circ w=\sum_{i,j,k}((f_i\circ g_j)\circ h_k)\otimes((a_i b_j)c_k)$ and $u\circ(v\circ w)=\sum_{i,j,k}(f_i\circ(g_j\circ h_k))\otimes(a_i(b_j c_k))$. These are equal termwise by associativity in $\mathcal C$ and $A$. The identities give $(\mathrm{id}_L\otimes1)\circ(\sum_i f_i\otimes a_i)=\sum_i f_i\otimes a_i$ and $(\sum_i f_i\otimes a_i)\circ(\mathrm{id}_K\otimes1)=\sum_i f_i\otimes a_i$ by the two identity laws in $\mathcal C$. The Hom modules and the bilinearity from step 1 now meet precisely the definition of an $A$-linear category, proving (2).

proof.text: The canonical maps on Hom modules $f\mapsto f\otimes1$ are $R$-linear by [def-weil-module-base-change], where $R$ acts through $R\to A$. With the identity object map they preserve identities by the chosen identities, and $Q(f\circ g)=(f\circ g)\otimes1=(f\otimes1)\circ(g\otimes1)$ since $1\cdot1=1$. These equations give a functor, and its Hom maps satisfy the definition of an $R$-linear functor. This proves (3).

source.place: Tags 00CV (algebra-section-tensor-product), 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product), 05G4 (algebra-definition-base-change); application to the raw Hom tensor product in def-weil-rationalization-karoubi

proof.text: For each $K,L$, $T$ gives an $R$-linear Hom map by [def-weil-linear-functor]. Its base change [def-weil-module-base-change] is a well-defined $A$-linear map $T_{K,L}\otimes_R A$ sending $f\otimes a$ to $T(f)\otimes a$. Use these maps and the object assignment $K\mapsto T(K)$. They send $\mathrm{id}_K\otimes1$ to $\mathrm{id}_{T(K)}\otimes1$. On pure tensors they send $(f\circ g)\otimes ab$ to $T(f\circ g)\otimes ab=(T(f)\circ T(g))\otimes ab=(T(f)\otimes a)\circ(T(g)\otimes b)$. For arbitrary finite sums both sides are $\sum_{i,j}(T(f_i)\circ T(g_j))\otimes a_i b_j$. Thus they define an $A$-linear functor $T\prime$.

source.place: Tags 00CV (algebra-section-tensor-product), 00CX (algebra-lemma-tensor-product), 05G4 (algebra-definition-base-change); application to the raw Hom tensor product in def-weil-rationalization-karoubi

proof.text: Here automorphism means a functor with a strict inverse $S=T^{-1}$ as in the statement. That inverse is $R$-linear: for $u,v:T(K)\to T(L)$ and $r\in R$, applying the bijective Hom map of $T$ to $S(u+v)$ and $S(u)+S(v)$ gives $u+v$ in both cases; applying it to $S(ru)$ and $rS(u)$ gives $ru$ in both cases. Every pair of objects has this form because $T$ is bijective on objects. Apply the construction in step 4 to $S$. On objects $S\prime T\prime$ and $T\prime S\prime$ are identities; on $\sum_i f_i\otimes a_i$, their maps are respectively $\sum_i S(T(f_i))\otimes a_i=\sum_i f_i\otimes a_i$ and $\sum_i T(S(f_i))\otimes a_i=\sum_i f_i\otimes a_i$. Consequently $S\prime$ is the inverse of $T\prime$. Finally both $Q\circ T$ and $T\prime\circ Q$ send $K$ to $T(K)$ and $f$ to $T(f)\otimes1$, establishing the stated equality and (4).
